edit.at: What if you could see how many lives

power.look: a small dark pill with a coloured outline that pops in with a burst just above each person's head
power.rule: a small number appears above each person's head, showing how many lives they have already lived

science.claim: Dr. Ian Stevenson documented 2,500+ cases of children reporting past-life memories at the University of Virginia.
science.source: Full script (approved); Stevenson, University of Virginia Division of Perceptual Studies
science.working: Real research cited in the full video; the 1-minute sample states the premise and the tick-down rule only.

script.text: What if you could see something about other people that they'd never know you could see? Alex walks up to Sam. Hey. Nice sweater. Oh, hey. Thanks. Above Sam's head — a number. Twelve.
Other students pass — 3, 7, 2, 9. Some have no number at all. Alex stares, fascinated.

I invented the lifesight detector. It's my own design. No one else has one. When I wear it, a small number appears above each person's head. A dark pill with a colored outline, almost touching the top of their head. It shows how many lives they've already lived. Reincarnation. Call it what you will.
The numbers vary. Most are single digits. Some are higher. The number ticks down when a life is spent. Used up. Passed.
What if you could see how many lives everyone has lived?
